title: LIVE LIGHT POLLUTION
source_name: NASA VIIRS Black Marble annual nighttime-lights composite via NASA GIBS (Román et al., Suomi NPP VIIRS Day/Night Band)
variable: Annual artificial nighttime brightness distribution (VIIRS DNB composite visualization, relative brightness index)
what: Environmental artificial night-sky brightness around the Great Lakes from NASA's VIIRS Black Marble annual composite: a continuous surface showing where city glow and development illuminate the night most strongly and where genuinely dark skies remain. Bright cores mark metropolitan light domes; dark blues mark the darkest shorelines and waters.
field: Light-pollution science (a branch of environmental photometry and ecology) studies artificial skyglow from electric lighting: it disrupts circadian rhythms in wildlife and humans, wastes energy, and erases natural starlight. Satellite day/night-band radiometry separates artificial glow from natural night-sky brightness (moonlight, airglow, starlight), mapping an environmental pressure distinct from any single observatory or preserve boundary.
